newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. Southern Command to leave Panama in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southern Command to leave Panama in June.

text.p: The U.S. military's Southern Command will start moving from Panama to Miami in June, its commanding officer Gen. Wesley Clark said Friday.
"By mid-September we will have rebased completely and moved to our new headquarters," Clark said in a written statement in Spanish.
About 2,000 soldiers and 3,200 family members are expected to move to Miami as part of the move.
Southern Command is the regional unified command responsible for all U.S. military activities in Central and South America south of Mexico.
The 1977 Panama Canal treaty requires the U.S. military to leave Panama by Dec. 31, 1999.
